models.observations: Twin stepped towers have legible glass belts, planted ledges and a shared cut-stone gate. A lamp, fountain and tiny trees give scale beneath the gold caps.

The ring, sunken competition floor and gate standards carry across all three ages. At native size a front pilaster crosses an arched recess, leaving dark fragments on its flanks and a stray outlined cap above.
defects: Separate the outer-wall buttresses from the applied arched bays. Align each buttress between bays or omit the bay hidden behind it, then inspect the full circumference.

models.observations: The longer glazed viewing canopy and gold parapet read at 64 pixels, including Ascension. Glazed arch outlines leak around the center-front stone buttress and break its surface.
defects: Move the buttresses between glazed arch bays or omit the underlying bay where they coincide.

models.observations: Brick turns to pale concrete in Modern and both keep the short northern roof and gold lip. The buttress in the foreground is flanked by short dark slivers from its overlapping decorative doorway.
defects: Separate buttresses from arch treatments, especially the forward visible sector.

models.observations: The curled flame holds up at 64 pixels and the stacks of spare fuel and listening stools give it a communal scale. Dawn and Bronze keep the same dark bench masses and central rim, leaving little age signal at phone size.
defects: Use a clearly age-responsive atlas material on a substantial shared surface such as the bench seats, backs or broad hearth ring to separate Dawn and Bronze.

models.observations: The pale raised court, gilded hearth and little clan standard distinguish this ceremonial version. The open front leads between carved posts toward the tall flame.
Four short pillars visibly support a second roof over the speaking terrace. The central rune, lectern and flanking lamps make the forecourt legible through the darker Medieval palette.
The bright blue roof lantern floats visually above a thick slab with visible wall support. The lectern still reads beneath the glazed porch and pale stairs define the entrance.
A brick vault rises through the iron roof platform and sits visibly behind the porch pediment. The industrial and concrete-modern versions retain the low colonnade and stepped entrance.

The pitch, lights and tall blue cantilever read as sports facilities. At phone scale the tiny front chevrons disappear and the bare linear stands have little dwarf-specific civic identity, particularly beside the preceding era.
defects: Develop a substantial stepped gatehouse or public scoreboard with a large dwarf emblem. Give the future structure a distinct glazed arch or crown visible at phone size.

models.observations: The charcoal cover shades narrow tiers beside the green pitch, with adequate raking supports. At 64 pixels the tiny chevrons and ticket lintel merge into the front parapet; the two long stands read as a generic sports venue.
defects: Enlarge the gate into a hewn dwarf civic entrance or scoreboard with a readable rune and supporting stepped masonry.

models.observations: The copper-hooped tun rests in a thick cradle beside the low hall. Its tap, projecting tankard sign, window box and warm door lamps can be found again in the Renaissance version.
The glazed vault and gold-clad metal tun make the brewing hall clear from above. The centered entry step, tap and little sign survive both Information blue and Ascension gold.
The tall brick flue and low roof monitor frame the broad wooden tun. Paired glowing windows, tankard sign and planted sill remain legible accents on the Modern concrete wall.
Two curved seating banks face a covered stone stage through an open aisle. The mask, paired curtain ties and stage lamps read as theater even when the Medieval roof darkens.
The tall blue proscenium, clipped pillars and gold mask sit clearly above the short semicircular benches. Glazing brightens in Ascension while the stage apron keeps its warm material.
The shallow iron roof and small rear flue distinguish the brick stagehouse. The central aisle and front stairs give the audience a clear route, and the face mask carries at thumbnail size.
Reopened all three ages. The front arches have intact outlines and clean stone between the jambs and adjacent piers. The gate standards and competition stone remain visible.
The glazed outer recesses are now clear of the buttresses in both palettes. Their regular rhythm follows the curved lower wall under the blue or gold canopy.
Moving the pilaster into the empty bay produced clean brick and concrete surrounds. The freestanding gate and judges’ roof still frame the central competition floor.
The new backrests, dark-to-ochre hearth rim and changing earth terrace separate Dawn, Bronze and Iron at 64 px. The carved posts and firewood remain clear of the entry.
The large gate with a hammer seal anchors the foreground. A gold roof arch traces the upper blue grandstand and remains visible in the Ascension palette.
The projecting stepped gatehouse and hammer seal read against the long ticket wall. The coal-dark roof, orange seating rows and small pitch lights still identify the industrial ground.

rounds.inspection: Inspected every listed asset’s authored age previews at phone scale, rendered all three serialized LODs at 64 px and inspected LOD1 at two angles. Compared neutral 64 px renders of all available eras in each audited family. Verified fragment metadata, shared material and atlas, triangle budgets and ratios, surface findings, orientation and local shape duplication against the reviewed files.

models.observations: The unequal stacks of glazed floors give the paired towers a strong outline, and the green vault directs the eye to the pedestrian door. The setbacks, straight wall piers and door surround stay attached in LOD1.

A forked flame rises well above its stone ring and the backed benches face it at different angles. Bronze and Iron darken the seating without dulling the fire. The bench legs, fire bed and seating circle remain coherent at LOD1.

The pale polygonal hearth and short stone seats give this gathering place a different perimeter from the timber campfire. Two upright standards frame the sightline. The middle mesh keeps the seats joined to the base around the flame.

At phone scale the curved tiers wrap the open field and the two separated blue canopy wings frame a tall scoreboard. That enclosing stand reads differently from the Industrial straight grandstand in both unpainted views. The roof posts and entry break survive LOD1.

The roofed grandstand sits along one side of a rectangular pitch, opposite a low entrance wall. The orange seats read through the dark roof at 64 px. The gate and long supporting frame remain distinct in the middle mesh.

The chimney over a simple pitched inn and the wall-sized cask make a clear sign for the tavern. The bracketed front sign, doorway and thick roof overhang survive the middle mesh in both Medieval slate and Renaissance tile.

The bright canopy and metal cask remain legible, but the unpainted outline still repeats the Industrial monitor, chimney, side barrel and sign in the same locations. The middle mesh preserves the cask cradle, overhang and door.
defects: Rebuild the future tavern around a different gathering space, such as a recessed tap court with a bridge and tanks, so its massing separates from the Industrial cask-house at 64 px.

models.observations: The flat roof monitor and taller flue distinguish the working brewhouse from the earlier plain roof. The thick side barrel and wall-hung sign identify the inn at LOD1. Industrial brick and Modern metal both leave the door and sign readable.

rounds.critic: Independent repair critic, second visual review of Dwarf, Orc and Saurian revisions
rounds.inspection: Compared the serialized LOD0 of each revision with available era siblings in two neutral 64 px views. Inspected every authored age preview, all three LODs at 64 px, and the front, side and rear of each model in colour at 190 px. Rechecked LOD1 from front and rear, serialized metadata, triangle and ratio budgets, exposed surface findings and shell orientation.

models.observations: Two exterior tables and tap handles on the paired brew tanks mark an open drinking court. The covered taproom and the tanks have separate foundations and clear wall contact. In grey the court replaces the older chimney inn and cask. The tables and tanks remain distinct at LOD1.

rounds.critic: Independent visual critic, frozen middle-LOD fidelity review
rounds.inspection: Inspected current age previews and all three serialized LODs at phone scale. Examined the middle mesh from the front, side and rear at larger scale and compared individual entrances and surfaces against LOD0. Rechecked the serialized catalog metadata, triangle ratios, exposed surfaces and shell orientation. Existing design scores were retained for unchanged designs that remained legible.

models.observations: The rear of each stepped tower has a full wall under every projecting slab. At the front the green entry canopy and its door remain readable beneath the two unequal towers.
The meeting circle keeps its low, backed benches, broad fire bed and upright fork of flame. Looking behind the fire shows the seats and stone ring still touch the ground.
The square-ended stone seats remain separate and supported around the hearth. The two standards and the flame survive the change of distance.
The long grandstand still has an uninterrupted roof above its orange seating and a full back wall. The pitch and the gate on the opposite side remain open.
The pitched tavern roof lands on both full side walls. Its chimney, side cask, hanging sign and dark central door still identify the inn at 64 px.
The taller flue and raised roof plate remain seated in the broad roof, alongside a legible cask and wall sign. The dark front door is clear against the masonry.
